items.title: Jaylen Brown’s decade with the Celtics prepared him for the Sixers’ spotlight
items.content:
PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 6: Jaylen Brown #7 of the Philadelphia 76ers talks to the media at Francis J. Myers Recreation Center on August 6, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images	Spending a decade with the Boston Celtics prepared Jaylen Brown for just about everything.

He now brings that experience to a rebuilt Philadelphia 76ers team seeking its first championship in 43 years.

Fully cognizant of the implications that come with playing in Philadelphia — a long-storied Boston rival — and alongside a star-studded group featuring Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, V. J. Edgecombe and LeBron James, Brown feels prepared for what’s ahead.

That’s all he’s focused on, fully aware of the spotlight his arrival — and James’ — will shine on both him and the Sixers this upcoming season.

“At this point now, I’ll probably ignore a lot of it,” Brown told reporters during his introductory press conference Thursday, per NBC Sports Philadelphia.

Brown, when asked, avoided most Boston-related questions from members of the press. He kept his answers short and measured, offering minimal insight when asked about his relationship with Jayson Tatum and feelings on the trade. 

But when the discussion steered toward the pressures that await him in Philadelphia, Brown expressed confidence. The past decade in Boston not only allowed Brown to improve as a player, but also forced him to learn how to handle the pressure that comes with chasing an NBA championship.

PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – AUGUST 6: (L-R) President of Basketball Operations Mike Gansey of the Philadelphia 76ers, Jaylen Brown #7, and managing partner Josh Harris pose for a picture at Francis J. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty ImagesHe’s already been through that, taking home both the Eastern Conference Finals and NBA Finals MVP awards in 2024.

It just so happened that Brown’s departure from the Celtics — something that had been rumored for the past seven-ish years — delivered him his next challenge at the perfect time.

“I played in Boston for the last 10 years, and the pressure is high there — it’s Titletown,” Brown continued. “They expect to win every single year, and they’re always looking for someone to blame. Some of those years, it was me. So I’ve been through that. All I come with is my work ethic, my mentality, impact on winning, and that’s just my approach. Nothing else matters.”
